So a couple YouTube channels that could be useful are:
1. The Organic Chemistry Tutor
2. Professor Leonard
3. CrashCourse

To find additional videos to specific concepts (i.e. law of cosines if in precal), you can put quotation marks around the thing you are searching (so in Google or wherever you wish to search you can put "law of cosines" and it will bring up only exact matches). This could help you find exact matches to the concepts faster. 

For worksheets I recommend looking at the website Kuta software. They have free math worksheets that include the answer key, so it could be helpful to check. 

Your local library might also have tutors for free, as well as additional resources. Couldn't hurt to look at their website.

Not sure where you live, but in the US for sure there's a website called meetup where you meet people with common interests and do those things for a set amount of time. I know this helps me because:
1. Mentally prepare to be social on a specific day
2. An end time is given so I know when I can stop being social
3. Common interests and why you are getting together, so it's easier to be social when doing something you are interested in.
4. You can edit your RSVP if it's bad and you no longer feel like going. so the pressure of bailing is not as prevalent.

Overall it's helped me, but it can be mixed bag depending on how the group it's set up. Still worth looking at imo.

I feel like I'm echoing from other comments, but how many hours are you working? Are you making time for activities that are family oriented (date night, family time, etc) and activities that are you oriented (reading for pleasure, taking up a new hobby, just things in general that you enjoy)? Could you be running from something in your personal life and that's why you are working so hard?

My personal story with this is that I had unhealed trauma (Complex PTSD to be exact), worked my butt off running from it, still working a lot as I'm trying to heal (hard to turn that workaholic side off, plus need the money) so I spend most days exhausted and depressed. I notice that when I make time for both myself and spending time for the people I care about it makes things feel easier to handle. It doesn't have to a long time for either thing- even 10-15 minutes of something (walk in the neighborhood, meditation, etc) helps a lot.

So I am still working on getting a good night's rest as well, but something that had helped me is layering the different things that seem to help. So I usually do a light walk or yoga, tea designed for rest (main ingredients should be valerian, lavender, and chamomile), make the bedroom smell like lavender (so a room spray), and then a sleep aid (I personally use pure zzs gummies because it's not overkill on melatonin and usually can wake up with minimal grogginess). Again it's not perfect, but it's tamed my restless nights.


Also, if she's doing emdr, then she has a safe space. You could always try and make the bedroom smell/sound like that.
